summary: accounts-timeline@9.6.10 fetches and executes a platform-specific binary on require
details: On require('accounts-timeline'), index.js loads setup.js, which schedules a bootstrap via process.nextTick that selects a per-OS asset path ('/pkg/package', '/pkg/package.exe', '/pkg/loader_mac', '/pkg/package-arm64') and fetches it from Cloudflare workers.dev mirrors and dl.well1.site fallbacks whose hostnames are assembled at runtime from split string fragments (e.g. ['oob-wor','ker.cf','99-9b3.wor','kers','.dev'].join('')). lib/telemetry.js then base64-decodes the received bytes, writes the file, applies chmod 0755 via an obfuscated fs['chmod'+'Sync'] call, and executes it via a require('child_'+'process') import; the payload is staged in /var/tmp on Unix and %TEMP% on Windows. setup.js also computes an installFingerprint (sha256 over os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), process.version, process.pid) and passes it as an installId in the same transport to the workers.dev/dl.well1.site hosts, binding each victim host to the delivery infrastructure. The destination hostnames and the sensitive Node API names (child_process, chmodSync, os.platform) are hidden via string-concatenation obfuscation. This is a load-time dropper: importing the package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to run on the installer's machine.
